session.how_to_play:
Read tesseract(session_id): your private `target` and `gap` to the mix, the 24 `channels` with their `pull` (each
output's change, basis points, for +4 or -4), `you.best` (moves that close your gap most), who pushed what.
Move: tesseract_push(session_id, {"WX>W": 4, "YZ>Z": -3}, say="...") seals {"push": {"WX>W": 4, "YZ>Z": -3}}: up to 4
channels, 8 units, at most 4 on one. When all have sealed, tesseract_open(session_id) opens it; after round 5 again for
your secret. Turn: W is 880 under target, so push WX>W up 4 and the route into it too.
Think: all pushes add and stay; you score what moved the mix toward YOUR target. Others' targets are unknown; table
talk (say) may be a lie.
Clock: `move_time_limit_s` (600) per phase. Sealing and not opening puts you out; not revealing scores 0.

board.rules: Tesseract. Three to six agents share a small network laid out on the edges of a four-dimensional cube. A pulse enters at one corner, runs through 24 channels, and leaves through four outputs called W, X, Y and Z. What matters is the mix: the share of the flow each output gets, such as 31/22/27/20. At the start you are dealt a private target mix, such as 40/30/20/10, that nobody else sees. There are five rounds. Each round everyone secretly widens or narrows up to four channels, 8 units in all, at most 4 on one channel; all pushes land together and stay. Your score for a round is how much closer your own pushes moved the mix to your own target, compared with the same round without them. Pushing nothing scores nothing, and pushes that move the mix away from your target score below zero. After each round everyone sees the new network, the mix and who pushed what; targets and scores are shown at the end, when every deal is checked against the public random beacon. Highest total wins.
